jurisdiction_note: Singapore tax resident individual who is a Singapore Citizen buying their FIRST residential property (so Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty is 0%; a second property would attract 20%). Singapore has no capital gains tax and dividends from Singapore companies are tax-exempt under the one-tier system, so equities face no tax at all, only broker and exchange fees.

meta.source_title: Ministry of Manpower — Income summary table (2025 median gross monthly income of full-time employed residents SGD 5,775 incl. employer CPF, ≈ SGD 5,000 excluding)
meta.note: low ≈ below-median full-timer, mid ≈ above-median professional, high ≈ senior professional in the 19.5% bracket. Bands are chargeable income after reliefs.

meta.source_title: IRAS — Resident tax rates from YA 2024 onwards
meta.note: Personal reliefs and one-off income tax rebates ignored.

ingress.label: Brokerage on purchase
ingress.plain_english: Singapore has no stamp duty on buying listed shares or ETFs electronically. A typical online broker charges around 0.1% to buy, which we treat as a cost rather than a tax.

meta.source_title: SGX — Retail investors (brokerage is set by the broker; 0.1% assumed)
meta.note: Assumption, consistent with the other countries. 9% GST on brokerage ignored.

ingress.label: SGX clearing and trading fees
ingress.plain_english: On top of brokerage, every SGX trade carries a 0.0325% clearing fee and a 0.0075% trading access fee charged by the exchange, together 0.04% of the amount invested. These are exchange fees, not taxes.

meta.source_title: SGX — Revised securities market fee structure (clearing fee 0.0325% of contract value, uncapped, from 1 June 2014)
meta.note: 0.0075% trading access fee corroborated by DBS and OCBC published fee schedules (2025). GST on fees ignored.

ingress.label: Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD)

meta.source_title: IRAS — BSD rates for residential property on or after 15 Feb 2023

ingress.plain_english: Buying any property in Singapore triggers Buyer's Stamp Duty, a one-off tax on a sliding scale of the price: 1% on the first SGD 180k rising to 6% above SGD 3m. On a SGD 1.3m home it comes to about SGD 36,600, roughly 2.8%.

meta.note: Charged on the higher of price or market value; assumed equal.

ingress.label: Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) — citizen, first property
ingress.plain_english: Singapore adds an extra stamp duty on top of BSD depending on who is buying. A Singapore Citizen buying their first residential property pays 0%, which is what we model. The same citizen buying a second home would pay 20%, and a foreigner 60%.

meta.source_title: IRAS — ABSD rates from 27 April 2023 (SC first property: not applicable; SC second: 20%; SPR first: 5%; foreigner: 60%)
meta.note: Modelled at 0% as the investor's first residential property. Shown so the 20%/60% cliff is visible in the drill-down.

ingress.label: Conveyancing and title registration
ingress.plain_english: Legal fees for the conveyancing lawyer plus the Singapore Land Authority registration fee for the transfer, treated as a flat cost rather than a tax.

meta.source_title: SLA — Fees for property registration services (transfer registration SGD 68.30; lawyer's fees vary, SGD 3,000 all-in assumed)

growth.label: Income tax on net rent
growth.plain_english: Net rent, after deducting expenses such as property tax, maintenance, agent and management fees, is added to your other income and taxed at your marginal rate every year.

meta.source_title: IRAS — Income from property rented out
meta.note: Expenses fixed at assumptions.property.cost_rate (25%) of gross rent rather than IRAS's optional 15% deemed-expense method. Property tax (modelled separately below) is also deductible in practice; that interaction is ignored, which slightly overstates income tax.

growth.label: Property tax (non-owner-occupied residential)

meta.source_title: IRAS — Non-owner-occupier residential tax rates from 1 Jan 2024 (12% on first SGD 30k of Annual Value, 20% next 15k, 28% next 15k, 36% above 60k), re-expressed on property value
meta.note: Derivation: Annual Value (AV) is the estimated gross annual rent, taken as 3.5% of value (assumptions.property.yield). Each AV threshold is divided by 0.035 (30,000 → 857,143; 45,000 → 1,285,714; 60,000 → 1,714,286) and each AV rate multiplied by 0.035 (12% → 0.42%, 20% → 0.70%, 28% → 0.98%, 36% → 1.26%). If the user changes the yield in the UI this schedule does not move.

growth.plain_english: Singapore charges an annual property tax on the Annual Value, the rent the home could fetch in a year. For a rented-out home the rate is progressive from 12% to 36% of that rental value. On a SGD 1.3m property renting at 3.5% that is about SGD 6,700 a year, roughly 0.5% of value, rising as the value grows.

meta.note: Approximation: AV assumed equal to 3.5% of market value; IRAS assesses AV from comparable rents and it is typically a little below achievable rent.

egress.label: Seller's Stamp Duty (sold within 4 years)
egress.plain_english: Singapore has no capital gains tax, but selling residential property within 4 years of buying triggers Seller's Stamp Duty on the full sale price: 16% in year one, 12% in year two, 8% in year three and 4% in year four. After 4 years there is nothing to pay.

meta.source_title: IRAS — SSD for residential property acquired on or after 4 July 2025 (16% / 12% / 8% / 4% over 4 years; previously 12% / 8% / 4% over 3 years)
meta.note: Simplification: the engine applies a single rate, so the 4th-year rate (4%) is used for any sale within 4 years. A 1-year horizon would really attract 16%. Holding period measured from the purchase date.

egress.label: Selling agent commission
egress.plain_english: Sellers in Singapore commonly pay their property agent around 2% of the sale price plus GST. The regulator sets no fixed rate, so it is negotiable, but it is a cost rather than a tax.

meta.source_title: Council for Estate Agencies — Commissions (no fixed or standard rate; 2% assumed)

property_leverage.plain_english: Mortgage interest is deductible against rent from that property. A rental deficit cannot be offset against your other income.

meta.source_title: IRAS — Guide to Form B1 (rental deficits)
meta.note: Treated as lapsing; IRAS guidance does not allow set-off against other income.
